image_description: A close-up, eye-level view of a dilapidated prison cell interior looking out through a heavy, rusted iron barred gate. The walls are made of crumbling concrete or plaster with significant peeling paint and exposed rough textures. The gate consists of vertical and horizontal iron bars, showing signs of age and corrosion. Through the bars, a brighter outdoor area with hints of greenery and another building structure is visible in the background.

The vertical bars of the gate show very slight inconsistency in thickness and alignment towards the top, and the background geometry seen through the bars is somewhat ambiguous/melted, though this could also be due to depth of field.

To verify the spatial relationship between the foreground gate and the background elements, checking for bleeding or incorrect depth cues through the bars.
To ensure the individual bars are distinct, continuous entities without merging into the frame or each other, and to check edge sharpness against the wall.

Boundary definition between the gate frame and the surrounding wall

Geometric coherence of the background visible through the bars
